findings.title: The "ask" handoff outcome immediately deletes the trial
findings.problem: When guestHandoff returns "ask", this branch clears both trial copies and shows "Welcome back" without asking anything. There is no Add/Discard choice. This contradicts the documented handoff contract and permanently removes trial answers that have not been saved into the account.
findings.failure_scenario: A student completes the trial and signs into an older account—even one with no saved progress. guestHandoff returns "ask"; the app deletes localStorage and sessionStorage copies, imports nothing, and gives the student no opportunity to retain the work.
findings.fix: Keep the trial intact while presenting an explicit Add/Discard decision. Clear it only after a confirmed save containing the accepted answers, or after an explicit Discard. Implement the accepted merge without overwriting existing account history; mergeGuestIntoBlob currently refuses accounts with answers, so changing only this UI branch is insufficient.

findings.title: The Add/Discard integration tests assert silent non-merge instead
findings.problem: The test named "Add merges once" never locates an approval prompt or clicks Add. It expects the original 30 rows, unchanged XP, no imported miss schedule, and a deleted trial copy. The adjacent "asks first; Discard" test likewise never exercises either control. These tests pass while the critical handoff behavior they claim to cover is entirely absent.
findings.failure_scenario: The implementation deletes every returning student's trial without asking, and both purported consent/merge regression tests remain green—as demonstrated by their current assertions.
findings.fix: Assert that the decision dialog appears and that no trial data is cleared beforehand. Exercise Add and Discard separately. Add must verify the imported answer identities and deterministic progress changes, plus idempotency on reload; Discard must verify unchanged account progress and explicit removal of the device copy.

findings.title: Raw schedule fallback ignores an already-classified owner
findings.problem: scheduleEntry accepts a raw numeric schedule whenever the visible catalog has one question with that number and there is no unresolved row. It does not reject a date whose history has already been classified as another source. rekeySchedule deliberately leaves dates belonging to case steps under their raw number, so this fallback can assign those dates to unrelated bank questions.
findings.failure_scenario: A legacy miss on sepsis step 101 receives a numeric due date during deriveMissSchedule. Classification correctly names the row "case:case-sepsis-1" because bank question 101 belongs to a different category. rekeySchedule leaves the raw date untouched because the owner is a case. With bank question 101 as the sole visible question numbered 101, scheduleEntry returns that case date, and Today/Review Misses serves the unrelated bank question as a scheduled review.
findings.fix: Permit numeric schedule fallback only when ownership is genuinely unscoped and uniquely established, or when the classified owner matches the requested canonical key. Never attach a classified case's date—or another source's date—to the visible question merely because its number is unique there. Add a regression covering a classified case row, an unrelated bank row with the same number, and a raw due date.

assessment: Do not release yet. The trial handoff silently deletes student work, and its integration tests explicitly accept that behavior while claiming to test Add/Discard. The identity migration also still allows a case-step review date to attach to an unrelated bank question. Findings are based on the supplied code; tests were not executed.
